title: Polity: Facts related to President, Vice president, Prime Minister, Chief minister, Parliament houses, cabinet ministers, attorney general etc. (Past Year Questions)

questions.q_en: In India, which of the following bills CANNOT be introduced in the Rajya Sabha?
options_en: Both constitutional amendment and ordinary bills
questions.solution_en: Money bills cannot be introduced in Rajya Sabha. Money bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President.
questions.solution_hi: धन विधेयक (Money Bills) राज्यसभा में प्रस्तुत नहीं किए जा सकते। धन विधेयक केवल राष्ट्रपति की पूर्व सिफारिश से लोकसभा में ही प्रस्तुत किए जा सकते हैं।

questions.q_en: The oath of office to the Vice-President is administered by the ________.
questions.solution_en:
As per Article 69 of the Constitution, the Vice-President takes the oath of office from the President of India.

• Option 1: Chief Justice of India - Administers the oath to the President.

• Option 3: CAG - Not involved in the swearing-in process.

• Option 4: Prime Minister - Has no role in administering the oath.
questions.solution_hi:
संविधान के अनुच्छेद 69 के अनुसार, उपराष्ट्रपति पद की शपथ भारत के राष्ट्रपति से लेते हैं।

• विकल्प 1: भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश - राष्ट्रपति को शपथ दिलाते हैं।

• विकल्प 3: CAG - शपथ ग्रहण प्रक्रिया में शामिल नहीं।

• विकल्प 4: प्रधानमंत्री - शपथ दिलाने में कोई भूमिका नहीं।

questions.q_en: In India, who appoints the Advocate General of a State?
questions.solution_en: The Governor of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed as a Judge of a High Court to be Advocate General for the State.
questions.solution_hi: प्रत्येक राज्य का राज्यपाल ऐसे व्यक्ति को राज्य का महाधिवक्ता (Advocate General) नियुक्त करेगा जो उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश के रूप में नियुक्त होने योग्य हो।

questions.q_en: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts made the president bound by the advice of the council of ministers headed by the prime minister?
questions.solution_en:
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 made the President of India bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

• This amendment explicitly stipulated that the President shall act in accordance with such advice, thereby reducing the scope for the President to act independently or delay decisions made by the Cabinet. ​

• 46th Amendment (1982): Enabled states to levy sales tax on consignment transfers and clarified taxation of works contracts, hire-purchase, and goods.

• 48th Amendment (1984): Extended President's Rule in Punjab beyond one year due to ongoing militancy and unrest.

• 40th Amendment (1976): Included 36 additional laws in the Ninth Schedule to protect them from judicial review and clarified maritime jurisdiction.
questions.solution_hi:
• 1976 के 42वें संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियम ने भारत के राष्ट्रपति को प्रधानमंत्री की अध्यक्षता वाली मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह से बाध्य किया।

• इस संशोधन ने स्पष्ट रूप से निर्धारित किया कि राष्ट्रपति ऐसी सलाह के अनुसार कार्य करेगा, जिससे राष्ट्रपति के स्वतंत्र रूप से कार्य करने या मंत्रिमंडल के निर्णयों में देरी करने की गुंजाइश कम हो गई।

questions.q_en: Who is considered the highest law officer of a state in India?
questions.solution_en:
· Advocate General is the highest law officer in a state, as per Article 165 of the Indian Constitution.

· Attorney General - Highest law officer of India (Article 76).

· Chief Justice of High Court - Head of judiciary but not a law officer.

· Auditor General - Handles financial audits, not legal matters.

Thus, the correct answer is A) Advocate General.
questions.solution_hi:
• भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 165 के अनुसार, महाधिवक्ता (Advocate General) किसी राज्य का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी होता है।

• महान्यायवादी (Attorney General) - भारत का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी (अनुच्छेद 76)।

• उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश - न्यायपालिका के प्रमुख, परंतु विधि अधिकारी नहीं।

• महालेखा परीक्षक - वित्तीय ऑडिट संभालते हैं, कानूनी मामले नहीं।

अतः सही उत्तर A) महाधिवक्ता है।

questions.q_en: Which Article of the Constitution of India empowers a high court to issue a writ?
questions.solution_en: Article 226 of the Constitution empowers a high court to issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, certiorari, prohibition and quo warranto. The writ jurisdiction of the high court is concurrent with the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
questions.solution_hi: संविधान का अनुच्छेद 226 उच्च न्यायालय को बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण (habeas corpus), परमादेश (mandamus), उत्प्रेषण (certiorari), प्रतिषेध (prohibition) व अधिकार-पृच्छा (quo warranto) जैसी रिट जारी करने का अधिकार देता है। उच्च न्यायालय का रिट क्षेत्राधिकार सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के रिट क्षेत्राधिकार के साथ समवर्ती (concurrent) है।

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the benefits of the retired President of India?

A. The former President of India will also been titled to a monthly pension of ₹ 2.5lakh.

B. He/She is entitled to a secretarial staff comprising a private secretary, a personal assistant, an additional private secretary, two peons, and office expenses up to ₹1 lakh per annum.

C. He/She is also entitled to free highest-class travel any where in India, accompanied by one person, by rail, air, or steamer.
questions.solution_en:
· The former President of India will also be entitled to a monthly pension of Rs. 2.5 lakhs.

· He is entitled to a secretarial staff comprising a private secretary, a personal assistant, an additional private secretary, two peons, and office expenses up to Rs. 1 lakh per annum.

· As per The President's Emoluments and Pension Act, 1951, the retired President of India is entitled to free medical attendance and treatment.

· He is also entitled to free highest-class travel anywhere in India, accompanied by one person, by rail, air, or steamer.

· The President of India gets a salary of Rs. 5 lakh per month. A former President of the country who demits office wither after the expiration of his term or by resignation gets a pension at the rate of 50% of the emoluments of the President per month for the rest of his or her life.

· As per the 1951 Act, a retired President will, for the rest of his or her life will be entitled to use of a furnished residence (including its maintenance) without the payment of rent, two telephones (one for internet and broadband connectivity), a car or allowance to avail a car and one mobile phone with national roaming facility.

· The law also states that the spouse of the former President is entitled to get a family pension at the rate of 50 percent of what a retired President gets, for the rest of his/her life, in case the President dies in office, resigns, or demits office after the end of the term.

· The spouse of the former President of India is also entitled to medical attendance and treatment free of charge for the rest of his or her life. Such a spouse will be entitled to the use of a furnished residence without the payment of license fee.

· He or she is entitled to a secretarial staff consisting of a private secretary and a peon, and office expenses of up to Rs. 20,000 per annum.

· The spouse, quite like the retired President, is also entitled to a free telephone and a car, or such car allowance for the rest of his or her life, and is allowed 12 top class single journeys anywhere in the country by air, or steamer or rail, accompanied by a companion or a relative.
questions.solution_hi:
• भारत के पूर्व राष्ट्रपति को 2.5 लाख रुपये मासिक पेंशन का भी अधिकार होगा।

• वे एक निजी सचिव, एक व्यक्तिगत सहायक, एक अतिरिक्त निजी सचिव, दो चपरासी सहित सचिवीय स्टाफ तथा प्रति वर्ष 1 लाख रुपये तक कार्यालय व्यय के हकदार हैं।

• राष्ट्रपति परिलब्धि व पेंशन अधिनियम, 1951 के अनुसार, भारत के सेवानिवृत्त राष्ट्रपति को ये सुविधाएँ प्राप्त होती हैं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President's rule in any state?
questions.solution_en:
• Article 356 allows the President of India to impose President's Rule in a state if:

o The state government fails to function according to the Constitution.

o There is a breakdown of constitutional machinery.

• It has been controversial as it has been misused multiple times for political reasons.

• The S.R. Bommai case (1994) restricted its arbitrary use.
questions.solution_hi:
• अनुच्छेद 356 भारत के राष्ट्रपति को किसी राज्य में राष्ट्रपति शासन लगाने की अनुमति देता है यदि:

o राज्य सरकार संविधान के अनुसार कार्य करने में विफल रहती है।

o संवैधानिक तंत्र का विघटन होता है।

• यह विवादास्पद रहा है क्योंकि इसका राजनीतिक कारणों से कई बार दुरुपयोग हुआ है।

• एस.आर. बोम्मई मामला (1994) ने इसके मनमाने उपयोग को प्रतिबंधित किया।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT the qualification for the appointment of judges of the Supreme Court?
options_en: A judge of high court for at least five years
An advocate of Supreme Court for at least ten years
An advocate of high court for at least ten years
A distinguished judge in the opinion of the President
questions.solution_en:
• An advocate of the Supreme court for at least ten years is not the qualification for the appointment of judges of the Supreme Court.

• ​According to Article 124(3) of the Constitution of India, the qualifications required for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court are as follows:​

○ Citizenship: The individual must be a citizen of India.​

○ Judicial Experience: The individual must have served as a Judge of a High Court (or of two or more such courts in succession) for at least five years.​

○ Advocacy Experience: Alternatively, the individual must have been an advocate of a High Court (or of two or more such courts in succession) for at least ten years.​

○ Distinguished Jurist: The individual is, in the opinion of the President, a distinguished jurist.​
questions.solution_hi:
• सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में कम से कम दस वर्ष तक अधिवक्ता रहना, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों की नियुक्ति हेतु योग्यता नहीं है।

• भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 124(3) के अनुसार, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश हेतु नियुक्ति की आवश्यक योग्यताएँ इस प्रकार हैं:

○ नागरिकता: व्यक्ति भारत का नागरिक होना चाहिए।
